title: Cistercian further Roman correction: 1606 and 1657 paired witnesses

traditions.label: Cistercian
traditions.scope: Printed missals of the Cistercian Order
traditions.coverage_note: Two early modern revised states; three complete Ordinary prayer pairs. Their prefaces describe the broader reforms.

stages.label: 1606 Romanizing Cistercian missal
stages.scope: Printed order missal implementing Roman conformity in the Canon while retaining Cistercian usages elsewhere.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum Sacri Ordinis Cisterciensis, Paris, Dionysia Cavellat, 1606; BSB 2 Liturg. 205 a
stages.summary: The 1606 Annotanda attributes full Roman conformity in the Canon to the 1601 and 1605 general chapters, and conformity elsewhere only as proper Cistercian use allows. The printed Ordinary still has a short Confiteor, a combined Suscipe Trinitas offering, and Orate/Dominus sit response.

evidence.claim: Explicit reforms of the 1601 and 1605 chapters; full conformity in the Canon, limited conformity elsewhere.
Three bounded prayer units directly transcribed from page images.

stages.limitations: This is already a revised state, not a proxy for all medieval Cistercian practice. The exact 1606 witness has now been split from the earlier broad printed-witness cluster. No claim that every decree of 1601 or 1605 was fully received locally.
stages.reception: The book identifies itself as for the Cistercian Order and invokes chapter authority; no monastery-by-monastery reception census has been made.

stages.label: 1657 further Roman correction
stages.scope: Printed Cistercian missal following the 1651 commission; a substantially Romanized Ordinary while retaining order-specific material.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cisterciense iuxta Romani recogniti correctionem, Paris, Sebastianus and Gabriel Cramoisy, 1657; Krzeszów copy, FIDES 3755
stages.summary: The Ordinary enlarges the Confiteor with named saints including Bernard and triple culpa; replaces the old Orate and response; prints separate host and chalice offerings and a revised Suscipe Trinitas after Lavabo. The Monitum reports reordered Pentecost-to-Advent Sunday Masses and Roman rubrics, but expressly retains differences in the graduals.

evidence.claim: The general chapter held in May 1651 authorized three learned men to correct the books; the 1655 mandate extends the printing privilege.
Primary description of the new revision; retained graduals prevent complete Roman imitation.
Three complete paired prayers and their position in the offertory read from images.

stages.limitations: The 1651 commission, 1655 mandate, and 1657 publication are distinct dates. The inspected 1655 instrument is not a universal effective-date decree. The Monitum historical catalogue of earlier defects must not all be assigned specifically to 1606.
stages.reception: The Cistercian superior authorizes the edition and printing monopoly; this is evidence of intended order use, not uniform local implementation.

transitions.summary: Further Romanization changes three complete Ordinary prayer units and the printed Holy Saturday ending: expanded Confiteor, replaced Orate and response, revised and relocated Suscipe Trinitas, and relocation of Spiritum nobis from a Postcommunio heading to the integrated Vespers sequence.

evidence.claim: The Holy Saturday ending changes presentation and rubrics: the 1606 book labels Spiritum nobis as Postcommunio; the 1657 book explicitly omits Postcommunio and supplies the same prayer after integrated Vespers. This is not proof that Cistercians omitted Vespers in 1606.

The Holy Saturday ending changes presentation and rubrics: the 1606 book labels Spiritum nobis as Postcommunio; the 1657 book explicitly omits Postcommunio and supplies the same prayer after integrated Vespers. This is not proof that Cistercians omitted Vespers in 1606.
The earlier state already implements Roman conformity under the chapters of 1601 and 1605.
The 1651 chapter ordered renewed revision; the editor claims a closer Roman form but retains differences in the graduals.

transitions.limitations: Text-collated applies to three complete prayer units, their local rubrics, and the Holy Saturday ending on the identified pages. The Holy Saturday quotations are bounded excerpts, not complete service transcriptions. Wider calendar, lectionary, and chant changes have primary-description evidence and have not been exhaustively collated. This is an institutional Cistercian revision relation, not proof that the 1657 typesetter directly copied this particular 1606 edition. All six complete prayer bodies have passed independent image review; one printed accent was corrected. The Holy Saturday rubrics remain a separate bounded review.

gaps.missing: Complete paired medieval or 1486–1487 Ordinary against 1606, and original chapter acts of 1601 and 1605.
gaps.next_source: USUARIUM 423 early printed missal; editions of the chapter acts for 1601 and 1605; BL Add. 46203 and Fribourg L158.
gaps.consequence: Cannot treat 1606 as an unchanged medieval baseline or date the first introduction of every Romanizing element.

gaps.missing: Complete collation of Pentecost-to-Advent readings, new feasts, exceptions in the graduals, and the Holy Week sequence.
gaps.next_source: 1606 BSB bsb10496382 temporale and calendar; 1657 FIDES 3755 Monitum and the complete corresponding sections.
gaps.consequence: The Monitum supports claims labelled primary-description; three complete Ordinary prayer pairs and the bounded Holy Saturday ending have direct paired image inspection.

gaps.missing: Local reception chronology and binding effective-date instruments.
gaps.next_source: Cistercian general chapter acts from 1651 onward, house book inventories, and correction orders.
gaps.consequence: Publication does not prove instant uniform replacement throughout the Order.
